Deletes the project entry; no IntelliJ chord confirmed; shares Delete with deleteForward, the pane scope decides

Ctrl+Shift+NumPad + cannot be told apart from a plain key in a terminal; F4 expands the project tree here
Ctrl+Shift+NumPad - cannot be told apart from a plain key in a terminal; Alt+C collapses the project tree here

Pane header options menu; no IntelliJ chord confirmed

Opens the selected file in the project pane; no IntelliJ chord confirmed; shares Enter with confirm and select, the focus decides

Undo

Copy the selection; in the editor Ctrl+C quits only when no text is selected (see docs/keymap.md)

Duplicate Line; with a selection it duplicates the caret line only and clears the selection, IntelliJ duplicates the selected text (docs/keymap.md)
Select All; the vim profile uses Ctrl+E because Ctrl+A is the Vim increment (docs/keymap.md)
Closes the editor tab; Ctrl+W is Extend Selection in IntelliJ, so it is not bound here

Select Previous Tab

Ctrl+Shift+F sends the same bytes as Ctrl+F in a terminal; Alt+F is kept here
Go to Line with the IntelliJ chord; the vim profile binds Alt+G instead (docs/keymap.md)

Narrows the project panel; no IntelliJ chord confirmed

Shrinks the bottom tool window; no IntelliJ chord confirmed
Switches the shell theme; Ctrl+T is Update Project in IntelliJ and stays here as the theme switch (docs/keymap.md)
IntelliJ uses Alt+F12 for Terminal (#364); Alt+2 stays as a second binding because the owner kept it, and the bare 2 is the shortcut while no input has focus
IntelliJ gives Maven no number; 9 is a number IntelliJ gives Version Control, which we do not have (#364)
IntelliJ gives no number to ACP Agents; 8 is a number IntelliJ gives Services, which we do not have (#364)
Open Settings is Ctrl+Alt+S in IntelliJ; it opens from the toolbar and the palette, and no chord is bound here yet
Connects to a running IntelliJ IDEA; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Run is Shift+F10 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the toolbar and the palette start the selected configuration
Debug is Shift+F9 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the toolbar and the palette start the debug session
Stop is Ctrl+F2 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the palette stops the current run
Refreshes the run configurations; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Chooses the run configuration; no IntelliJ chord confirmed on the reference page
Resume Program is F9 in IntelliJ; F9 is New Directory in the project pane, so the debugger keeps its own keys
Pause Program is not on the IntelliJ reference page; the debugger keeps its own keys
Step Over is F8 in IntelliJ; F8 stays free for the debugger work (docs/keymap.md)
Step Into is F7 in IntelliJ; F7 is New Project File in the project pane
Step Out is Shift+F8 in IntelliJ; unbound here, the debugger work decides
